investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-24T12:26:40Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production API's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm ELB endpoint at /v1/agents. Because the failure is shared across every sibling check with the exact same error message, the fault is localized to the swarm gateway layer that backs remote agent provisioning, not to any individual eval or check-specific code path.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable from the production API at the time of the eval run. Every call to POST /api/agents that requires remote agent provisioning received HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning". Because all three remote-agents checks depend on this single upstream provisioning call, all three failed with the identical message. No evidence of a prior passing run exists (lastPassingAt is null, previousRunCount is 0), so the duration of the outage cannot be bounded from eval history alone.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=455 > max 300)
investigations.summary: The eval check `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the published status snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 455 minutes old at the time of the eval run (2026-08-24T12:27:17.092Z), exceeding the contract maximum of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the snapshot freshness assertion alone.
investigations.rootCause: The observability snapshot published at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was not refreshed within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 455 minutes old when the eval ran, meaning the workflow or process responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json did not execute successfully for at least 7.5 hours prior to the eval. This is an eval-detected staleness condition; no evidence of a user-facing outage or live traffic impact is present in the supplied packet. The check is registered as non-required with statusImpact=informational (source: `source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383`), so this does not constitute a declared product outage.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=455, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='desktop-nightly-release', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — all other assertions passed; only the age threshold was breached.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — this is the exact contract boundary that was violated.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check registered as required=false, statusImpact=informational, staleAfterMinutes=360 — the registry staleAfterMinutes (360) is looser than the contract max (300), indicating a potential misalignment between registry config and expected-output contract.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed — the public website itself is reachable; the failure is isolated to the snapshot JSON freshness, not site availability.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2164-2172: runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from the payload — the runner correctly read a stale payload from the live URL.
possibleCauses: The workflow or automated process (source='desktop-nightly-release') responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json to https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run or did not complete successfully within the past 300 minutes, leaving a stale artifact in place.
The nightly release pipeline that publishes the snapshot was delayed, skipped, or failed silently, resulting in the snapshot not being updated on schedule.

A GitHub Pages deployment or publishing step succeeded in a prior run but the snapshot generation step upstream of it failed or was not triggered, so the previously published file was served unchanged.

There is a configuration misalignment: the feature registry sets staleAfterMinutes=360 while the expected-output contract enforces max=300 for snapshotAgeMinutes. If the snapshot is regenerated on a cadence between 300 and 360 minutes, the eval will fail even though the registry considers the check not yet stale.
